name: format_reference
description: The file format reference for boards, symbols and footprints, with examples. Read this before writing files.

name: check
description: Load the project and report errors and warnings for every item, or one item.

args.name: include_info
args.description: also list info notes

args.name: item
args.description: only this board, symbol or footprint

name: drc
description: Design rule checks of a layout. With list = true: every DRC rule with its id, category, severity, and whether it applies to this board and why. Without: the layout's diagnostics that carry a rule id. Rule ids go in the board's [drc] disable list or severity table.

args.name: name
args.description: layout or board

name: layout
description: Run the layout engine on a layout: the configured [engine] phases in order, then the score per term with the worst offenders of each. Phases not implemented yet are listed as skipped. With search it runs a beam search over the stages in memory: each kept engine state branches into children with different values of that stage's [engine.search] knobs (placement seeds by default), the best `keep` survive each stage from the global route on, and the winner is written with its settings pinned in [engine]. Use search instead of rerunning place and route by hand with different seeds.

args.name: dry_run
args.description: report without writing the plan

args.name: from
args.description: start at this phase

args.name: keep
args.description: with search, how many nodes survive each stage (default 4)

args.name: only
args.description: run one phase

args.name: search
args.description: true, or how many settings to try (default 16)

args.name: to
args.description: stop after this phase

name: fit
description: Find the smallest rectangular board a layout fits on. Loads the layout once and tries outlines of many aspect ratios in memory: the current placement scaled to the new size, edge connectors slid along their edge, holes kept in their corners, the rest legalised, routing demand estimated per tile; then checks the smallest sizes with the global router. strategy tight, balanced or spread sets the gap between parts and the routing room kept. width or height holds one side. write sets the board's [outline] size and writes the placement. Place the layout first: the search starts from its current arrangement.

args.name: aspects
args.description: width over height ratios to try

args.name: height
args.description: hold the height, mm

args.name: name
args.description: layout

args.name: verify
args.description: how many of the smallest sizes to check with the global router (default 3, 0 skips)

args.name: width
args.description: hold the width, mm

name: stackups
description: Stackup presets for a board's `stackup.preset`: JLCPCB and PCBWay builds and generic HDI builds with layer thicknesses and er. Filter the list, or give name to get one preset's layers.

args.name: fab
args.description: jlcpcb, pcbway or generic

args.name: layers
args.description: copper layer count

args.name: name
args.description: one preset, returns its layers

args.name: search
args.description: substring of name or description

args.name: thickness
args.description: finished thickness in mm, within 10%

name: edit
description: Edit a schematic (sch), layout (pcb) or board spec (board) with commands, one per line, in one load and one check at the end. It keeps the file's comments and layout and returns the check report of what it touched. A command that names a missing pin, part or net fails before anything is written. Send `help` alone for the commands of that target. Commands: sch add/remove/move/set/net/connect/disconnect/nc/unnc/note; pcb place/unplace/track/untrack/via/unvia/zone/unzone/cutout/uncutout/pair/text/fanout/stitch/watermark/title/test; board class/unclass/via/unvia/outline/cutout/stackup.

args.name: commands
args.description: one command per line, e.g. `add R1 R 10k --footprint R_0402_1005Metric` then `net MID R1.2 R2.1 --class Signal`

args.name: item
args.description: item name, optional when the project has one of that kind

name: list_items
description: Every board, symbol and footprint in the project with its file and error counts.

name: show_item
description: The resolved model of one item as JSON: pins with positions, expanded pad arrays, stackup with computed trace geometry, impedance and current analysis.

name: render_item
description: Render an item to PNG exactly as the viewer shows it and return the image. Without the side panels the image is cropped to the drawing, so width and height are the largest it gets.

args.name: canvas_only
args.description: drop the side panels

args.name: context
args.description: what happens to everything outside focus

args.name: focus
args.description: schematic or layout only: zoom to these parts, nets or pins (U1, SPI_*, U1.3) and fade the rest

args.name: hide
args.description: layers to turn off; hiding a copper layer with no copper in show shows every other copper layer

args.name: region
args.description: zoom to [x0, y0, x1, y1] in mm

args.name: rulers
args.description: label mm coordinates along the edges, to pick the next region

args.name: save_to
args.description: also write the PNG here, relative to the project

args.name: show
args.description: layers to turn on, e.g. F.Fab, F.Mask, In1.Cu

args.name: unit
args.description: symbol unit, 1 based

name: kicad_search
description: Search the installed KiCad libraries by name. Every word must match Library:Name.

name: import_kicad_symbol
description: Convert a KiCad symbol (Library:Name) into a .sym.toml in the project. with_footprint also imports its default footprint, or give footprint to pick one.

args.name: dir
args.description: relative to the project, default symbols/

args.name: footprint
args.description: Library:Name of the footprint to import and link

args.name: spec
args.description: Library:Name, e.g. Amplifier_Operational:LM358

name: import_kicad_footprint
description: Convert a KiCad footprint (Library:Name) into a .fp.toml in the project.

args.name: dir
args.description: relative to the project, default footprints/

args.name: spec
args.description: Library:Name, e.g. Package_SO:SOIC-8_3.9x4.9mm_P1.27mm

name: new_item
description: Write a starter file for a board, symbol, footprint, schematic, layout or sim, to edit from. A sim starts as an FDTD run of a layout, with sim_kind logic as a logic sim of a schematic (clock, reset, a clocked assertion), or with sim_kind circuit as an analog circuit sim of a schematic (a drive, an AC sweep and checks), whose nets you rename.

args.name: dir
args.description: relative to the project

args.name: sim_kind
args.description: with kind sim, default fdtd

name: trace_width
description: Minimum track width for a current (IPC-2221).

args.name: current
args.description: e.g. 2A or 500mA

name: run_sim
description: Run a simulation (*.sim.toml): an FDTD run of a layout on the GPU (ports on pads, lumped models for passives, S-parameters saved as JSON and Touchstone next to the spec), any other kind (dc, thermal, cascade, channel, pdn), or a logic sim of the schematic netlist (stimulus, assertions, setup and hold, a VCD next to the spec). Render the sim afterwards to see the plot or the waveforms.

name: serpentine
description: Points for a track that replaces a straight segment and adds a given length as trombone bumps to one side. Paste them into the track's points.

args.name: add
args.description: e.g. 2.5mm

args.name: from
args.description: x,y in mm

args.name: to
args.description: x,y in mm

name: tie
description: Tie every SMD pad of a plane net (a net with a [[zones]] entry) to the nearest plane layer with a short stub and a via beside the pad, away from the part body, and append them to the layout file. Use this for ground and supply pads instead of routing tracks between them; `route` with a glob skips plane nets.

args.name: nets
args.description: comma separated plane nets, globs allowed, default every net with a zone

name: route
description: Autoroute the ratsnest of the named nets of a layout on a grid, keeping each class's width, clearance, layers and via, and append the tracks and vias to the layout file. Existing copper is never moved unless reroute is set.

args.name: bend_cost
args.description: mm of track per 45 degree bend, three times that for 90

args.name: layers
args.description: comma separated copper layers, default all

args.name: nets
args.description: comma separated, * and ? globs

args.name: reroute
args.description: remove these nets' tracks and vias first

args.name: via
args.description: comma separated [[vias]] names from the board to choose from, default the class vias

args.name: via_in_pad
args.description: allow vias fully inside SMD pads (filled and capped); by default vias keep off every SMD pad

name: fill
description: Fill the zones of a layout and store the copper at the end of its file, so loads and the viewer skip the fill until the zone's copper, clearances or neighbours change.

name: tune
description: Length-match a layout: meander the short net of every pair over its skew limit and every match group member short of its target, on the longest segments where the bumps clear every other net, and write the points back into the tracks.

args.name: amplitude
args.description: largest bump height in mm

args.name: nets
args.description: comma separated globs, default all

args.name: pitch
args.description: bump pitch in mm

name: neck
description: Neck down track ends that enter a pad narrower than the track or break clearance near the pad: the end becomes a separate [[tracks]] entry with an explicit width, the smallest of the class width, the pad's smaller side and the widest that keeps clearance, rounded down to 0.01 mm, never under min_track_width and never longer than the class neckdown. taper steps the width down over a short chain of segments. Stored zone fills are refreshed.

args.name: nets
args.description: comma separated globs, default all

name: place
description: Place the layout's parts automatically as a quick start: connectors and edge-mount parts on the board edges (never an RF and a USB connector on one edge unless it must), mounting holes and fiducials in the corners, the largest chips near the centre, each IC's decoupling caps, crystal and pull-ups clustered at the pins they serve, placed by weighted wirelength, then legalised on a 0.05 mm grid with no courtyard overlaps and refined by simulated annealing. Writes at, rotation and side into [[footprints]] and refreshes the stored fills. Parts with locked = true stay put.

args.name: keep_placed
args.description: leave every part that already has a placement

args.name: parts
args.description: comma separated globs of the parts to place, default all

args.name: seed
args.description: default 1; the same seed gives the same placement

args.name: side
args.description: F, B or both, default F

name: silk
description: Move every silk reference that check flags to the clear spot it suggests, repeating until the labels settle, and optionally hide the ones that have nowhere to go. Writes label = { at, rotation } or hide = true into the footprints.

name: testpoints
description: Add a test pad to each net that needs probe access and has none: a TestPoint part (TestPoint_Pad_D1.0mm footprint, both written into the project if missing) joined to the net in the schematic sheet that lists it, a footprint on the probe side in free space near the net's copper, and an autorouted track and via from the net's copper. Nets default to the layout's [test] nets; impedance and pair nets are skipped.

args.name: nets
args.description: comma separated, * and ? globs, any case; default the [test] nets

args.name: pitch
args.description: grid and least spacing of the test pads, mm

args.name: side
args.description: probe side F or B, default the [test] side (B)

name: sparam
description: Analyse a finished sim or cascade: passivity and reciprocity, a TDR of one port (impedance against time with a Gaussian edge), mixed-mode Sdd/Scc/Scd for a pair given as IN+,IN-,OUT+,OUT-, and crosstalk FROM,TO in frequency and as a step.

args.name: rise
args.description: 10-90% rise, e.g. 35ps

args.name: tdr
args.description: port name or number

name: models
description: Find the 3D models (STEP or VRML) the project's footprints name, downloading missing KiCad library models into the cache. Reports each model's path and triangle count, or why it is missing.

name: fab
description: Write the fab package for a layout into a folder: RS-274X Gerbers (X2) per copper, mask, paste, silk and edge layer, Excellon drills, a zip of those for upload, BOM (generic and JLCPCB), pick-and-place, fab notes and assembly drawings. Refuses while the layout has errors.

args.name: out
args.description: output folder, relative to the project

name: export
description: Write a layout as one STEP assembly for enclosure CAD: the board as a solid with its drilled holes and cutouts, each part's STEP model embedded and placed, and VRML, generated and missing models as surfaces or boxes. Board bottom at z = 0, X and Y as the layout with Y up.

args.name: out
args.description: output .step file, relative to the project

name: parts
description: Price a layout's or schematic's BOM at Mouser, Farnell and DigiKey and find cheaper equivalents: the same part at another distributor, resistors and ceramic capacitors with the same value, package, tolerance, voltage and dielectric (never a downgrade), generic discretes (2N7002, S1D, SS14, SMAJ..) by name and package, indicator LEDs by colour and package, and the distributor's suggested replacement for parts going obsolete. Costs are at the needed quantity, buying up to a price break when that is cheaper. Keys come from ~/.config/agentee/distributors.toml ([mouser] api_key, [farnell] api_key and store, [digikey] client_id, client_secret and site).

args.name: distributors
args.description: mouser, farnell, digikey; default every one with a key

args.name: farnell_store
args.description: e.g. uk.farnell.com, ie.farnell.com, www.newark.com

args.name: name
args.description: layout or schematic

args.name: order
args.description: directory, relative to the project, to write order sheets to instead of returning the report: NAME-order.csv and NAME-<distributor>.csv, each with the lines to buy there first, then the lines bought at another distributor, then what it lacks

args.name: refs
args.description: only the BOM lines holding these references

args.name: spares
args.description: with order: 0402/0603 resistors and capacitors to the next 10 above need + 5, one spare per D, Q, U and F line, or the part's `spares` field

name: bom
description: BOM cost table of a layout or schematic: every line priced at Mouser, Farnell and DigiKey at each board count (default 1, 10 and 100), buying up to a price break when that is cheaper, with the total and the cost per board, and the lines that could not be priced and why. Use parts to look for cheaper equivalents.

args.name: boards
args.description: board counts, default [1, 10, 100]

args.name: distributors
args.description: mouser, farnell, digikey; default every one with a key

args.name: json
args.description: return the rows as JSON instead of the table

args.name: name
args.description: layout or schematic

name: datasheet_fetch
description: Fetch and cache a part's datasheet, or every part's of a layout or schematic, into the cache every project shares (~/.cache/agentee/datasheets). Tries the part's `datasheet` field, its symbol's `datasheet` URL, then the datasheet the distributors list for its mpn, with a browser user agent and retries. Lists the parts with no reachable datasheet: ask the user for those, never fill the gap from memory. A design fetch records the URL, hash and revision of each in datasheets.toml at the project root.

args.name: name
args.description: layout or schematic, a reference (U3), a symbol or a part number

args.name: refresh
args.description: fetch again even when cached

args.name: url
args.description: fetch one part from this URL instead

name: datasheet_text
description: Read a cached datasheet as text with page numbers, fetching it first when it is not cached. Use find for the pin table and electrical characteristics (e.g. find "VS" returns the passages holding that word, matched whole and case sensitive when it has capitals), and pages for a page range. Without find or pages it returns the first 3 pages and the page count.

args.name: context
args.description: lines around each match

args.name: name
args.description: a reference (U3), a symbol, a part number or a library part

args.name: pages
args.description: page or range, e.g. 4 or 4-6

name: datasheet_add
description: Add a PDF the user supplied (a part behind a login, a vendor that blocks downloads) to the shared datasheet cache under its part number.

args.name: path
args.description: the PDF, relative to the project

args.name: url
args.description: where it came from

name: library_list
description: The user's parts library: the connectors, regulators, passives and other parts they have chosen, each with its role, part number, rating, pin count, notes, whether it is preferred for its role, and its last checked stock and price. Look here first whenever a design needs a part, and use what is here before searching for anything new; ask the user before using a part outside the library for a role it covers.

args.name: role
args.description: connector, rf connector, usb connector, regulator, resistor, capacitor, led, diode, crystal ...

args.name: words
args.description: words that must all match, e.g. ["2-pin", "power"]

name: library_find
description: Search for a part: the library parts that match, and only when none does (or search is set) active parts in stock at Mouser, Farnell and DigiKey for the same words, merged by part number with total stock, the distributors that have it, the best unit price at the quantity needed and a datasheet link. Use it when the library has no part for a role; pick from the datasheets, then library_add the choice and library_use it.

args.name: need
args.description: at least this many in stock, default 1

args.name: role
args.description: only library parts of this role

args.name: search
args.description: search the distributors even when the library has a match

args.name: words
args.description: e.g. ["3.3V", "buck", "1A"] or a part number

name: library_add
description: Add a part to the user's parts library: its symbol and footprint (a .sym.toml/.fp.toml file, a project item or a KiCad Library:Name) and 3D model copied in, the footprint height set from the model, its datasheet fetched and pinned, its stock and price recorded. Notes say when the part is not in stock as an active part or has no datasheet. Add only parts the user agreed to, with the rating from the datasheet.

args.name: datasheet
args.description: URL or PDF, default the symbol's URL then the distributors'

args.name: footprint
args.description: default the symbol's footprint

args.name: generic
args.description: a resistor or capacitor series: any value on this footprint

args.name: local
args.description: into this project's .agentee/library

args.name: model
args.description: a STEP or VRML file or URL, default the footprint's model

args.name: name
args.description: library name, default the part number

args.name: preferred
args.description: the first choice for its role

args.name: rating
args.description: from the datasheet, e.g. "2 A, 100 V"

args.name: role
args.description: connector, regulator, resistor, capacitor, led, diode, crystal ...

name: library_show
description: One library part in full: its symbol, footprint and model files and where each came from, its pinned datasheet file, and its stock and price at each distributor with the date checked.

name: library_use
description: Copy a library part's symbol, footprint and 3D model into this project and return the edit command that places it with its mpn, mfr and library fields.

args.name: force
args.description: replace project files that differ from the library copy

name: field_solve
description: Solve a trace cross-section with the GPU field solver: impedance, effective permittivity, C and L per metre, delay. Includes solder mask, thickness, coplanar grounds and differential pairs. Within 0.5% of exact references with fine = true.

args.name: gap
args.description: differential pair gap

args.name: netclass
args.description: take width and gaps from this class

args.name: sweep
args.description: loss sweep START,STOP,POINTS, e.g. 10MHz,20GHz,21: R, L, G, C, Z0 and dB/in per frequency with skin effect, stackup roughness and a causal (Djordjevic-Sarkar) dielectric

name: impedance
description: Trace impedance on a board layer for a width (and pair gap), or the width that hits a target.

args.name: board
args.description: board name, optional when there is one

args.name: coplanar_gap
args.description: gap to the ground pour either side, grounded coplanar on outer layers

args.name: gap
args.description: differential pair gap

args.name: target
args.description: e.g. 50ohm
